record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.original_question: Is there a Borel class of profinite groups whose isomorphism relation lies strictly between smooth equivalence relations and S_∞-complete equivalence relations under Borel reducibility, and in particular does this happen in the abelian case?

evidence.quote: Problem 18. Is there some Borel class of profinite groups with isomorphism relation properly between S∞-complete and smooth? In particular, how about the Abelian case? Update: The answer to this problem is yes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the standard Borel-equivalence-relation framework. For Polish spaces $X,Y$ and Borel equivalence relations $E$ on $X$ and $F$ on $Y$, write $E \leq_B F$ if there exists a Borel map $f:X\to Y$ such that $x\,E\,x' \iff f(x)\,F\,f(x')$. An equivalence relation $E$ is called smooth if $E \leq_B \mathrm{id}_{\mathbb{R}}$, and is called $S_\infty$-complete if it is Borel bireducible with the orbit equivalence relation of some Borel action of the infinite symmetric group $S_\infty$ that is universal among such actions (equivalently, Borel bireducible with the isomorphism relation on countable graphs).

A profinite group is a topological group that is isomorphic to an inverse limit of an inverse system of finite groups; equivalently, a compact, Hausdorff, totally disconnected topological group. The space of (codes for) profinite groups can be made a standard Borel space, and topological isomorphism is a Borel equivalence relation on this space. By a Borel class of profinite groups we mean a Borel-invariant Borel subset of this standard Borel space.

Question: Does there exist a Borel class $\mathcal{C}$ of profinite groups such that the topological-isomorphism relation $\cong$ restricted to $\mathcal{C}$ satisfies
$$\text{smooth} \;<_B\; (\cong \restriction \mathcal{C}) \;<_B\; S_\infty\text{-complete},$$
i.e. is strictly above every smooth equivalence relation and strictly below every $S_\infty$-complete one? In particular, does such an intermediate class $\mathcal{C}$ exist within the abelian profinite groups?

artifact.status_search_result: The problem list itself notes an update stating that the answer is yes: there exists such an intermediate Borel class of profinite groups. By Pontryagin duality, isomorphism of profinite abelian groups is Borel bireducible with isomorphism of countable torsion abelian groups, which is classifiable by Ulm invariants and lies strictly between smooth and $S_\infty$-complete, providing an explicit witness in the abelian case.

status_evidence.title: Oligomorphic groups, their automorphism groups, and the complexity of their isomorphism
status_evidence.snippet: For profinite, locally compact, and Roelcke precompact groups, complexity considerations of the isomorphism relation are studied.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work computes Borel complexity of isomorphism for profinite groups, supporting the existence of intermediate complexity classes.
